clue.text: So peacock may have appeared, over in Pennsylvania

indicators.note: in places the word for over inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
over, as in finished, means up (time is up)

explanation.surface: A peacock showing itself, finished with, somewhere in Pennsylvania.
explanation.walkthrough: The peacock here is the butterfly, which emerges from a chrysalis; 'in' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Before a peacock butterfly emerges it spends time as a chrysalis, the insect's resting stage.

clue.text: A type seen to make a profit?

parts.note: a, as in so much a head, means per
type means form or kind

explanation.surface: A question about whether a certain kind of person is seen to earn money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' means per (ten pounds a head). The question mark admits that to make a profit is only one way to do well, as shares that do well are said to deliver.
explanation.definitionFit: Investments that deliver good returns are said to do well, i.e. to earn money for their holders.

clue.text: Aircraft operator has change of heart, becoming kingpin

indicators.note: the central letter of the word for aircraft operator is swapped for another

parts.note: a pilot operates an aircraft

explanation.surface: A pilot who changes their mind and becomes the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has change of heart' swaps the middle L of PILOT for V.
explanation.definitionFit: A kingpin is the central point on which things turn, the linchpin of an operation.

clue.text: Stylishness displayed by US city? Not in the past

indicators.note: Not tells us the words for in the past are to be left off the city's name

parts.note: Chicago is a US city
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An American city once known for its style, but no longer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not' removes AGO from CHICAGO.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegance and fashionable flair is what the French-borrowed word means.

clue.text: Records originally kept in 13's home

indicators.note: kept in puts the first letter of records inside the moorland plant word

parts.note: the answer to 13 across is a heather, which gives heath

indicators.note: originally picks out the first letter of records

explanation.surface: Records first stored in a heather-lover's house.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 across is a heather, so 13 gives HEATH; 'kept in' puts R (the first letter of Records, from 'originally') inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fireside is the traditional symbol of family life and so stands for a household.

clue.text: North American girl entering the Promised Land

indicators.note: entering places the girl's name inside the biblical land

parts.note: Canaan is the land promised to the Israelites in the Bible
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A girl from America arriving in the land of milk and honey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' signals the girl going inside the biblical land.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the country north of the United States is a North American.

clue.text: Tasty noodle girl rejected

parts.note: noodle and sap both mean a fool

indicators.note: rejected tells us the girl's name is sent back, read in reverse

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: A delicious noodle dish turned down by a girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noodle' is not food but a fool, SAP; 'rejected' turns DI into ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapid is a formal word for flavourful, having an agreeable savour.

clue.text: Put oneself at risk, ducking the likely outcome?

definitions.meaning: a skater on fragile frozen water is likely to end up plunged into the water, ducked

explanation.surface: Someone takes a gamble while dodging the probable result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ducking' looks like dodging, but it means being dunked: going through thin ice is the likely outcome of the literal activity.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to behave in a way that courts danger, like skating where ice may break.

clue.text: One's out to get fare reduced

definitions.text: One's out to get fare reduced

parts.words: One's out to get fare reduced
parts.note: a person out of doors to eat food, who reduces the fare by eating it, rather than a passenger seeking a cheaper ticket

explanation.surface: A traveller is out to get a cheaper ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fare' suggests a travel ticket, but it is food taken on an outing, and eating it reduces it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eating an outdoor meal goes out with food and gets through it.

clue.text: Row, when one's attorney is held in contempt

indicators.note: is held in tells us the following pieces sit inside the word for row

parts.note: a row is a din, a loud noise
one's is I'S, written as IS
DA is a district attorney in the US

explanation.surface: A dispute in which a lawyer is found in contempt of court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link. 'held in contempt' reads as a legal phrase, but 'is held in' is the container signal and 'contempt' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorn and disdain are synonyms for a feeling that something is worthless.

clue.text: Ultimately no stress in this woman's demise?

definitions.text: Ultimately no stress in this woman's demise?

parts.words: Ultimately no stress in this woman's demise?
parts.note: in verse, a line whose final syllable is unstressed has a particular kind of close; read whimsically it is a lady's death

explanation.surface: A woman's death was peaceful at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: A prosody term for a line ending on an unstressed syllable, read as a woman's end.
explanation.definitionFit: In poetry, a line closing on an unstressed extra syllable is given this name.

clue.text: Mexican painter touring island in popular holiday area

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the painter's name surrounds the island letter

parts.note: Diego Rivera was a Mexican muralist

explanation.surface: A Mexican artist travels round an island in a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' puts I inside RIVERA.
explanation.definitionFit: The French and Italian Mediterranean coast is a classic sunny vacation spot.

clue.text: Sister takes a short time over subtle shades

indicators.note: takes means the sister holds the letter a within her

parts.note: a nun is a religious sister

indicators.note: over tells us the short time is turned round

parts.note: sec is short for second

explanation.surface: A nun taking a brief moment over delicate colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' signals the container and 'over' the reversal of the short time.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine distinctions of tone or meaning are delicate gradations.

clue.text: Was too clever for old union leader getting gently teased

indicators.note: leader picks out the first letter of union

parts.note: twitted means teased or taunted mildly

explanation.surface: Someone got the better of a former union boss who was being ribbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old union leader' reads as a trade union chief, but it splits into O and U.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone through cunning is to beat them for cleverness.

clue.text: A little daughter I called Heather

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A parent naming a small daughter Heather.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the botanical genus of heaths, the moorland plants.

clue.text: Yarn health official is first to spread about

parts.note: MOH is Medical Officer of Health
to air news is to make it known widely

explanation.surface: A health officer is first to put a story about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' looks like a tale, but it is thread spun from angora goat hair.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a thread or fabric made from angora goat fleece.

clue.text: So the rain battered a shrub

indicators.note: battered means knocked about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thus the downpour battered a bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' rearranges SO THE RAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a name for the hydrangea, a flowering bush.

clue.text: Almost becoming alarmed, say, in small vessel

indicators.note: Almost means the final letter is dropped from what the soundalike gives
say signals that the word is to be pronounced, giving a soundalike spelling

parts.note: panicking means becoming alarmed

explanation.surface: Nearly getting into a state inside a small boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives a soundalike of PANICKING and 'Almost' drops its last G. 'vessel' suggests a boat, but it is a small metal cup.
explanation.definitionFit: A pannikin is a small metal drinking cup or pan, a little container.

clue.text: Blunder involves joint being slightly salty

indicators.note: involves means wraps around, so the joint goes inside the word for blunder

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake
a rack of lamb is a joint of meat

explanation.surface: A mistake involving a joint that turns out a bit salty.
explanation.walkthrough: Bish is dated British slang for a mistake; 'involves' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Brackish water is somewhat saline, like a mix of fresh and sea water.

clue.text: Reportedly some African countries' source of fruit

indicators.note: Reportedly tells us the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: the Barbary States were the North African coastal countries

explanation.surface: News of where some African fruit comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: The Barbary States were the old North African coast countries; 'Reportedly' gives the soundalike.
explanation.definitionFit: The shrub bears small red edible berries, so it is a fruit-bearing plant.

clue.text: To be blunt, half one's wealth is — under one's belt

parts.note: bald means plain or blunt, as in a bald statement

indicators.note: half tells us only the first half of the word for wealth is used

parts.note: riches means wealth

explanation.surface: Frankly, half of someone's money is tucked under their belt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' keeps RIC from RICHES; the dash marks the truncation.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a sash worn over the shoulder to carry a sword, a kind of strap.

clue.text: Product of church, spoken or sung

parts.note: oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Something produced by a church, either spoken or sung.
explanation.definitionFit: Music for a choir is performed by voices singing together.

clue.text: Drag fish up on the sheltered side

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to draw is to drag or pull
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: Hauling a fish up out of the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns DRAWEEL into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side away from the wind, so protected from it.

clue.text: Fish in pastry dishes served round southern state

indicators.note: served round means the pies are placed around the state abbreviation

parts.note: pies are pastry dishes
SC is South Carolina, a southern US state

explanation.surface: Fish in pies offered around a southern state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served round' signals the container. 'Fish' is the zodiac sign, not seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign of the twelfth house is represented by two fishes.

clue.text: Legal right one retained to delay rise

indicators.note: retained means held inside, so the numeral one sits within the legal right

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A legal right was kept to postpone getting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retained' puts I inside LIEN; 'rise' is getting out of bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay in bed late is to put off getting up.

clue.text: Customers, given two keys, allowed man back inside

indicators.note: inside places the reversed pair within the two keys

parts.note: C is a musical key
E is another musical key

indicators.note: back tells us allowed and man are read in reverse

parts.note: let means allowed
Neil is a man's name

explanation.surface: Customers given two keys let a man back in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns LETNEIL into LIENTEL, which goes 'inside' C and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of regular buyers of a business is its patronage.

clue.text: Chapter in uplifting story — a brilliant display

indicators.note: in places the chapter abbreviation within the reversed story
in a down clue uplifting means the story is read upwards, in reverse

parts.note: a tale is a story

explanation.surface: A chapter in an inspiring tale makes a dazzling show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' turns TALE into ELAT, and 'in' puts C after its E.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is conspicuous success or a dazzling show of style.

clue.text: He composed operas, Lawrence appearing in one

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence enlisted under the name Ross
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A composer of operas, with Lawrence appearing in one.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) served in the RAF as Aircraftman Ross.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini wrote The Barber of Seville and other Italian operas.

clue.text: Part of ear domestic fowl ignores in meadow

indicators.note: ignores tells us the word in is dropped from the breed of fowl

parts.note: a Cochin is a breed of domestic chicken
lea is a poetic word for meadow

explanation.surface: A part of the ear that a farmyard bird ignores in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores in' drops IN from COCHIN, a chicken breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The cochlea is the spiral cavity of the inner ear.

clue.text: Go like the clappers, in production of this sound …

definitions.text: Go like the clappers, in production of this sound …

parts.words: Go like the clappers, in production of this sound
parts.note: go like the clappers usually means rush, but here clappers are bell tongues producing a ringing noise

explanation.surface: Rush off, making this noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Go like the clappers' is British slang for going very fast, but here the clappers are bell clappers striking.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the loud ringing note of metal striking metal, as a bell makes.

clue.text: … army entertainer

definitions.meaning: a great multitude, especially an army
one who receives and entertains guests

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a large armed multitude and someone who welcomes guests.

clue.text: Endlessly con boss

indicators.note: Endlessly means the last letter is cut off the word for con

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A never-ending con played on the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'con' looks like a swindle but is the old verb to study.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob, like a decorative stud.
